title: Garlic Butter Steak Skillet
seoTitle: Fast Philly Cheesesteak Skillet | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Cheesy steak without the wait
description: Cheesy steak without the wait. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

ingredients.name: Deli roast beef or shaved steak

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Garlic Butter Steak Skillet in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat the flat-top
steps.instruction: Preheat cast iron or flat-top to medium-high. This is a shift-night shortcut — speed over perfection. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Sear beef and peppers
steps.instruction: Sear shaved beef with frozen pepper-onion mix 6–8 minutes until beef edges crisp and vegetables soften. Season with salt and pepper. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Melt provolone
steps.instruction: Lay provolone slices over the hot beef and pepper mixture; cover the skillet 1 minute until cheese melts into the meat and starts to lace the pan edges.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Garlic Butter Steak Skillet onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Load hoagies
steps.instruction: Pile into toasted rolls. Fast Philly Skillet feeds the hall in under twenty minutes. Target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Garlic Butter Steak Skillet — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Prep all mise en place before the bell — this meal wins on organization, not speed hacks.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Fast Philly Cheesesteak Skillet with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Fast Philly Cheesesteak Skillet on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Cheesy steak without the wait. A hall pick for tight shifts — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Minimal prep — chop aromatics before shift change so you can cook as soon as the board quiets.
